claims.statement: Focused second-language instruction can produce substantial target-oriented learning gains, so a near-A0 method should not assume that unguided exposure alone is the most efficient route for all linguistic targets.
claims.limitations: Meta-analytic effects are target- and test-oriented; they do not prove broad communicative proficiency or one optimal instructional package.

claims.statement: Explicit instruction tends to outperform implicit instruction on many studied L2 outcomes, but the size and interpretation of that advantage depend strongly on how explicitness and learning outcomes are operationalized and measured.
claims.limitations: Short treatments and controlled tests can favor explicitly accessible knowledge; this does not establish that explicit instruction alone produces spontaneous implicit ability.

claims.statement: Evidence that explicit instruction improves controlled grammatical knowledge cannot automatically be generalized to implicit, spontaneous or automatized knowledge because these constructs require different measurement conditions.
claims.limitations: The explicit/implicit knowledge distinction and its measurement remain theoretically and methodologically contested.

claims.statement: Comprehension-based and production-based instruction both facilitate L2 development, with relative advantages depending on whether the target outcome is receptive or productive and on retention interval.
claims.limitations: The strongest comparative evidence is grammar-focused and should not be generalized unchanged to every skill or linguistic subsystem.

claims.statement: Processing Instruction is particularly useful for changing problematic form-meaning processing during comprehension, but its advantage does not justify replacing production practice when productive performance is the target outcome.
claims.limitations: Effects vary by target processing problem, learner age, explicit information, strategy training and outcome task.

claims.statement: Production practice has a distinct instructional role: when productive knowledge is the target, production-based practice can equal or exceed comprehension-based instruction on delayed productive measures.
claims.limitations: Production is not automatically beneficial merely because learners speak or write; task quality, feedback, target accessibility and practice conditions matter.

claims.statement: Interaction facilitates L2 development by creating opportunities for comprehensible/modified input, negotiation, feedback, attention and modified output; its benefits should not be reduced to exposure time or conversation volume alone.
claims.limitations: Interaction studies vary in interlocutor, task, target feature and measurement; causal contribution of each mechanism is not identical across studies.

claims.statement: Corrective feedback can support L2 development, but feedback effectiveness is moderated by feedback type, task/context and learner variables; no one feedback form should be universalized across skills and learners.
claims.limitations: RQ-025 must provide the dedicated cross-skill feedback synthesis before Nếp defines a global feedback policy.

claims.statement: Deliberate and systematic practice can make L2 processing faster, more stable and less effortful, but automatization is not equivalent to simply repeating the same item faster.
claims.limitations: Automaticity is difficult to measure; speed alone may reflect task familiarity or simple speed-up rather than broader automatic processing.

claims.statement: The declarative-to-procedural-to-automatic account of Skill Acquisition Theory has meaningful empirical support, including recent direct evidence for a three-stage trajectory under explicit learning and intensive comprehension practice, but its generality to natural English learning and other instructional conditions remains unresolved.
claims.limitations: The direct test used 73 learners and a deliberately learned miniature language; it cannot establish a universal sequence for all L2 learning conditions.

claims.statement: Usage-based accounts provide strong reasons to treat language learning as developing form-meaning/function constructions from exemplars whose frequency, salience, contingency and prototypicality matter; raw frequency alone is not a sufficient teaching rule.
claims.limitations: These sources synthesize a broad theoretical/empirical program rather than provide one comparative trial against rival global theories.

claims.statement: For adult L2 learners, frequent exposure may fail to establish low-salience or L1-blocked grammatical cues, so usage-rich instruction can still require deliberate attention or form-focused support.
claims.limitations: Which forms require explicit support, at what point and for which Vietnamese learners must be determined by feature-specific evidence and learner data.

claims.statement: Visual/textual enhancement can increase perceptual salience but has only modest average effects on L2 development and can compete with meaning processing; making a form bold or otherwise noticeable is not evidence that the learner processed or learned its meaning/function.
claims.limitations: The evidence base is largely visual grammar input; other modalities and richer attention-directing tasks may behave differently.

claims.statement: Intentional vocabulary activities can produce relatively high immediate form/meaning learning rates but substantial forgetting remains, so deliberate lexical learning is efficient but does not remove the need for later retrieval, contextual encounters and use.
claims.limitations: The meta-analysis focuses on common word-focused activities and recall outcomes rather than broad contextual language use.

claims.statement: Incidental vocabulary learning from meaning-focused reading/listening/viewing is real but the proportion of unknown words learned from any one exposure period is limited and strongly moderated; incidental exposure therefore complements rather than replaces deliberate learning for beginners with limited time and vocabulary.
claims.limitations: Incidental vocabulary is only one language subsystem; the optimal balance with intentional learning depends on exposure volume, proficiency and target outcomes.

claims.statement: Sociocultural approaches add a distinct developmental construct—responsiveness to contingent mediation or learning potential—which should not be collapsed into current independent performance; supported performance can be diagnostically useful even when it is not evidence of independent mastery.
claims.limitations: Dynamic assessment evidence is heterogeneous and its psychometric reliability, scalability and use for self-study require separate validation in RQ-024.

claims.statement: No major evidence base reviewed in RQ-022 supports a single exclusive mechanism as sufficient for adult instructed L2 development; the strongest convergence is toward complementary conditions involving meaning-focused input, attention to form-meaning relationships, targeted instruction, opportunities for retrieval/production, interaction/feedback where relevant, and repeated practice over time.
claims.limitations: This is a cross-theory synthesis, not evidence for a fixed lesson sequence, dosage or one universal method.

claims.statement: For a near-A0 self-study system, a defensible provisional direction is meaning-first but not meaning-only, input-rich but not input-only, explicit when it solves a real processing/knowledge problem, production when productive ability is the target, interaction when contingent communication is the target, and scaffolding whose use is recorded separately from independent performance.
claims.limitations: This is not yet Nếp Method. Exact ordering, dosage, beginner exceptions, Vietnamese-specific moderators and cross-skill integration remain open through RQ-023–RQ-028 and target-learner validation.

claims.statement: The exact balance and sequencing of meaning-focused exposure, explicit explanation, processing work, productive retrieval, interaction, feedback, contextual variability and fluency practice cannot be derived from theory labels alone and remains an empirical curriculum/learner question.
claims.limitations: Explicit unresolved integration question for later method/curriculum synthesis.
